name: @devlensio/cli

tools.name: resolve_context
tools.description: Start here when you need to LOCATE a symbol or EXPLAIN how something works. One call returns a task-shaped packet: ranked nodes with one-line meanings, call flow in execution order, involved files, code bodies of the top 10 nodes, security flags, and an id map, within a token budget. FLOW edges carry the position inside the caller: -calls[#3]->  (repeats as [#1,#3]), executed-after-return as -calls[defer:X]->, parallel as -calls[conc]->, plus at=file:line for the real call site, so you do not need a second call to establish what runs in what order. NOT the right tool for dependency or impact lists: if the question is who calls/uses/imports X, what depends on X, or what breaks if X changes, call blast_radius instead - the packet shows one neighbourhood, not the complete dependent set. For a definition question the answer is the file that DECLARES the symbol (plus explicit re-exports); its callers and importers are context, not part of the answer. Sections are ranked and may be truncated; a TRUNCATED banner means call blast_radius or get_node for the rest. Intents: pinpoint, reference-list, flow, overview, concept, security-audit, exploratory (default). The repo is resolved from the working folder — no graphId needed.

task.description: The actual question or task, in plain words

focus.description: nodeIds, symbol names or filePaths to center the packet on

tokenBudget.description: 500..100000; default scales with repo size. Code bodies ride on top of this budget.

repoPath.description: Only needed when several repos are analyzed and the working folder is ambiguous

tools.name: find_symbols
tools.description: Cheap symbol lookup by name, path fragment, or concept words (lexical BM25F). Returns ranked nodeIds with path:line refs — no code, no structure. Use it to locate a symbol; use resolve_context when you need meaning, flow, or code.

query.description: Symbol name, identifier, path fragment, or concept words

summaryType.description: Which summaries to weight in ranking, default both

tools.name: get_node
tools.description: Full detail for ONE node: technical/business/security summaries, callers (who uses it), callees in execution order (what it calls, with #n, line and control-flow markers such as await, defer:X, conc, repeat, maybe), and its own call sites. Pass a nodeId from resolve_context/find_symbols, or a symbol name to auto-locate. include=['code'] adds the raw source (first 120 lines; page with codeLines=[start,end]). Prefer this over reading whole files.

node.description: nodeId, or a symbol/file name to locate first

include.description: Default: summaries + callers + callees. Add 'code' for raw source.

codeLines.description: With include:['code'] — absolute 1-based [start, end] file lines. Defaults to the first 120 lines of the node; max 400 per call. Follow the banner's next hint to page.

edgeTypes.description: Restrict callers/callees to these edge types

tools.name: blast_radius
tools.description: Use this for EVERY dependency or impact question: who calls X, who uses X, who imports X, what depends on X, what breaks if X changes, every reference to X, callers/consumers of X. It returns the COMPLETE reachable set as compact file:line refs, not a ranked neighbourhood, which is why it answers these questions when resolve_context cannot. Default direction is UPSTREAM (the dependents that break); direction='downstream' is what X itself depends on. radius controls hops (default 2; hub-fanout auto-caps at 1 unless explicit). Pass from+to commit hashes instead of a target to diff two analyzed commits with per-change impact. If the question enumerates files and the answer needs more than ~5 of them, this is the tool, not grep. When the question is which files use/call/import X, answer with EXACTLY the files this returns (plus the declaring file only if the question also asks where X is defined). Do not add files from a resolve_context packet that this list does not contain.

target.description: nodeId, symbol name, or file path (required unless from/to given)

direction.description: Default upstream (who depends on it). 'both' runs both traversals.

radius.description: Hops. Default 2, capped at hub fanout; explicit value is uncapped.

from.description: Older commit hash — commit-range diff mode

to.description: Newer commit hash — commit-range diff mode

diffRadius.description: Blast-radius hops for changed nodes in diff mode. Default 1.

tools.name: repo
tools.description: Manage analyzed graphs. action='list' shows analyzed repos (one line each); action='analyze' indexes a repo folder (run once per repo, or after large structural changes); action='freshness' compares the graph to the current HEAD; action='health' reports summary coverage and circular-dependency groups. Repo resolved from the working folder when omitted.

path.description: For analyze: local repo path (or GitHub URL with isGithubRepo=true)

isGithubRepo.description: For analyze: path is a GitHub URL

instructions:
WHAT THIS IS
DevLens gives you a precomputed structural graph of a TypeScript/JavaScript/React/Next.js/Node.js
codebase. Nodes (components, hooks, functions, routes, stores) are connected by typed edges.
Every node carries TECHNICAL, BUSINESS and SECURITY summaries, and tool responses are plain
line-oriented text (no JSON to parse).

ROUTING RULE (important)
For ANY where-is-it / how-does-it-work / what-does-this-mean / who-depends-on-it question, call
resolve_context FIRST — do not start with grep/read. The packet answers in one call what would
otherwise cost several grep+read rounds. Grep only for exact-string sweeps DevLens cannot do
(e.g. finding every literal occurrence of a string constant).

THE FIVE TOOLS
  resolve_context(task, intent?)  — THE front door: ranked nodes with one-line meanings, call flow,
      involved files, code bodies of the top 10 nodes, security flags, id map. Start here.
  find_symbols(query)             — cheap BM25F lookup; ranked nodeIds with path:line refs.
  get_node(node, include?, codeLines?) — one node's summaries/callers/callees; include=['code'] for source,
      codeLines=[start,end] pages long bodies by absolute file lines.
  impact(target|from+to)          — what breaks if this changes (upstream) / what it depends on
      (downstream) / commit-range diff impact.
  repo(action)                    — list / analyze / freshness / health for the graph itself.

NO graphId NEEDED: the graph is resolved from your working folder. Pass repoPath only if several
repos are analyzed and the folder is ambiguous.

FRESHNESS
If the user has UNCOMMITTED changes, node/line data may lag the working tree. Structure refresh is
cheap, summaries are expensive: run repo(action='analyze') to refresh structure and inherit old
summaries for unchanged nodes; treat newly added nodes as 'no summary yet'.
